failingTests: task 1: the masthead is valid JSX with a computed service count
task 2: Panel renders its title and children, and a missing team falls back to Unassigned
task 3: StatusBadge lives in its own module with named status labels
task 4: incident counts and maintenance notes appear only when they exist
task 5: the status filter buttons narrow the visible cards
task 6: one click of Run checks performs all three regional checks
task 7: acknowledging an incident updates the card and the log immutably
task 8: hiding a card keeps details state with the right service and lists down services

cleanup.notes: Setup (npm ci in tests/) creates tests/node_modules with the pinned Vitest, Testing Library and React packages; the optional dev setup (npm ci in starter/) creates starter/node_modules. Cleanup deletes both; the tests create nothing else, write no files and store nothing in the browser. Resetting the learner's work means restoring starter/src from a fresh copy of the lab. The expected output file writes variable timings as <ms>, and test file lines may print in any order. The 25-minute median and 30-minute cap are planning figures for the module's guided lab slot, not a measured learner pilot. Setup (the one-time npm ci) completes before the lab slot's working time; the 30-minute allowance covers only work on the tasks. All assertions are behavioral: Testing Library queries against rendered output, React's own console warnings for HTML attribute spellings (task 1) and a call-through spy on the StatusBadge module's default export (task 3); no test reads the learner's source text. Partial-objective note: usestate#o3's predict-the-rendered-value clause and props#o1's destructuring-default form (a || fallback renders the same text) are not lab-tested; both are practised on their topic pages, not in this lab.
